title: Actus et consecratio crismatis in cena domini
shelf_note: A liturgical manuscript (Missal leaves: Maundy Thursday chrism rubric, Gloria, Canon 'Te igitur', Pater noster with square notation; Houghton shelfmark label 'fMS Typ 309' visible on the slides). No tradition or collection is given, and Mass liturgy sits outside the library's core esoteric/early-science shelves; the title is only the rubric of the first leaf, not the name of the manuscript.
structure_note: The three images are not consecutive leaves: image 1 is fol. 2r (pencil '2' bottom right) and ends mid-Gloria at 'Quo[niam]'; image 2 starts at the Canon 'Te igitur' (Credo, Preface and Sanctus missing between them); image 3 is fol. 12v (pencil '12v' in the margin), the Pater noster after the Canon. The images look like a set of 35mm slides of selected openings, so the 'book' is a selection of leaves, not a continuous text; a reader paging through will meet unannounced jumps. None of the three pages has a translation (translation is null on all three).

ocr_errors.problem: nomen sacrum expanded and spelling normalised to 'Christi' (scribe writes 'cristi'); same for 'Iesu Christe' for 'ihu xpe'

other.note: The <image-desc> says the initial 'N' contains 'a bird (likely a pelican) feeding its young'. The image shows no pelican: the uprights of the N are two columns that end in siren/merfolk figures with human faces, and the diagonal is a fish- or dragon-like creature. The decoration description is invented.
No translation: translation is null for this page.

ocr_errors.ocr: haec dona haec munera haec sancta sacrificia
ocr_errors.image: Hec do-na ✠ Hec mu-nera ✠ Hec san✠cta
ocr_errors.problem: medieval 'hec' normalised to classical 'haec'; similarly 'que' → 'quae'. Meaning unchanged

other.note: The initial 'T' is described as 'a stylized cross or liturgical instrument'. It is a column/crucifix-like figure with a winged head at top and two serpents or dragons at the base. Vague but not clearly false.
No translation: translation is null for this page.
<vocab> tag lists '1540', which is not on the page (it comes from the catalogue date).
No translation: translation is null for this page.

book_verdict: The transcription is very good on all three leaves, with abbreviations expanded and spelling lightly normalised. But the page-1 image description invents a pelican in the initial, nothing is translated, and the 'book' is a non-consecutive set of slides of a Houghton missal manuscript whose fit to the shelves is doubtful.
